description.en: This experiment is used to verify Thevenin's Theorem by determining the Thevenin equivalent voltage (VTH) and resistance (RTH) and comparing the calculated load current with the observed load current.
Use these controls to view instructions, use AI Guide, auto-connect the circuit, check connections, add readings, calculate results, reset the experiment and generate reports.
Automatically creates the required Thevenin circuit connections. After auto connection, use CHECK to verify the wiring.
Set the values of RL, R1, R2 and R3 using these sliders before taking observations.
Turn ON the power supply after successful connection verification. The display shows the applied source voltage.
Adjust the source voltage and record the corresponding VTH, RTH and IL values.
The voltmeter measures voltage, the ammeter measures load current and the digital multimeter is used to measure equivalent resistance during verification.
Connect the circuit according to Thevenin's Theorem. Terminal numbers can be used to create or remove wire connections.
All recorded values of VTH, RTH, RL and IL appear here. Multiple observations can be taken using different resistance settings.
Calculate the load current using IL = VTH / (RTH + RL) and compare it with the observed value to verify Thevenin's Theorem.
Open this panel to view all equations used in the experiment including VTH, RTH and IL calculations.
Generate and download the experiment report after completing observations and verification.
